Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation and pilot plan

Thanks for the call this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before I pull together the pilot statement of work. High level notes from our discussion: 

- Target workload: live streaming inference for clinical note summarization (tokenized average ~320 tokens per request).
- Latency targets: p95 streaming end-to-end <= 120 ms for the 32-token tail; p50 ~40 ms.
- Throughput / concurrency: baseline planned steady throughput ~180–220 req/s, burst concurrency up to 40 concurrent sessions during peak windows.
- Model family: you mentioned a preference for a 70B open model variant; we should validate memory footprint vs KV cache sizing.
- Data residency: must remain in us-east and be SOC2-compliant for pilot.

Proposed immediate next steps (please confirm):
1) Orbit to share a representative workload sample and one week of request-rate histogram (format: NDJSON or CSV).
2) Redwood to produce a hardware/throughput shortlist (H100 vs A100 vs L40S) with reserved-throughput estimates and pilot cost.
3) Agreement on acceptance criteria for the pilot (p95 latency, sustained throughput, error rate).
4) Schedule a 30–45 min pilot kickoff (engineering only) next week to review perf test harness and telemetry.

Attachments: I’ll accept your workload file and will attach a short SLO template to propose acceptance criteria once I have the sample.

If that looks right I’ll draft a pilot scope and send a one-page PO template for procurement.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer

Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity performance validation and pilot plan (internal hardware shortlist)

Internal notes and proposed capacity plan based on Orbit sample and targets:

Summary assumptions (from Orbit sample):
- Avg token/request: 320 tokens, peak 800 tokens (rare).
- Avg request size gives average inference time weight; streaming tail must be preserved.

Shortlist and expected reserved throughput per pod (conservative estimate with live-streaming CPU + GPU overhead):
- H100 80GB (2x pods reserved): estimated steady 220 req/s total, p95 ~95–115 ms (streaming enabled, KV cache on prefix), warm KV cache assumed.
- A100 80GB (3x pods reserved): estimated steady 180 req/s total, p95 ~120–140 ms.
- L40S (2x pods reserved): estimated steady 160–180 req/s, p95 ~130–160 ms.

Recommendation: Pilot on H100 with fallback A100 capacity policy. Rationale: H100 gives headroom on p95 and lower burst latency; A100 is an acceptable fallback when H100 pool capacity is constrained. During pilot we can test kernel/quantization profiles to reduce memory and improve throughput.

Proposed acceptance criteria for pilot (to include in SOW):
- p95 streaming latency <= 120 ms across a 24-hour run at 75% of target steady throughput (i.e., 165 req/s).
- Sustained error rate < 0.5% (model failures, timeouts).
- No more than one failover event from H100->A100 during 72-hour stress window.

Operational ask: Marissa, can you own test harness and telemetry dashboards for the pilot? Ben, can you draft the reserved throughput pricing and include delta H100->A100? I attached a quick cost worksheet with placeholder numbers (gpu-cost-estimate.xlsx).

Thanks —
Lauren
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation and pilot plan

Alex — thank you for the sample and histogram. Based on the workload and internal sizing discussion below, here’s the recommended pilot plan and immediate asks so procurement can move quickly.

Pilot summary (proposed):
- Scope: Dedicated pilot on H100 80GB reserved pool (2 pods) with A100 80GB on-demand fallback policy.
- Target acceptance criteria (finalized): p95 streaming latency <= 120 ms over a 24-hour continuous run at 75% of steady target (165 req/s), error rate <0.5%.
- Pilot duration: 7 days (3 days smoke tests + 4 days sustained/scale tests).
- Expected capacity: baseline 220 req/s sustained headroom; burst concurrency up to 40 sessions validated during stress tests.
- Deliverables: perf report, telemetry dashboards, kernel/quantization recommendations, cost delta summary.

Procurement asks: please review the attached one-page PO template and confirm any procurement-specific clauses we should pre-load (billing contact, billing cadence, legal review timeline).

Next meeting: Let’s schedule the engineering kick-off on Tue 21 Sep at 10:00 ET (30 min). Agenda: test harness, shared telemetry endpoint, rollout/fallback policy, and SLO gating.

If Procurement confirms PO fields and Alex confirms kickoff, we’ll send the SOW and onboarding calendar invite.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
